info.title: MICROSERVICE_PROD_Refund Management API
info.description: The Refund Management API provides a streamlined mechanism for handling refund requests within the payment processing system. Through this API, businesses can efficiently cancel or reverse transactions by specifying the unique refund identifier. This functionality is essential for merchants and financial institutions managing accounts or customer service interactions. Typical consumers include customer support teams and financial reconciliation processes that require accurate tracking of refunds. The API ensures automated processes, enhancing the user experience and operational efficiency.

delete.summary: Delete a specific refund by its identifier.
delete.description: This operation allows you to delete a specific refund record using its unique identifier. It is important to ensure that the refund is no longer needed before deletion, as this action cannot be undone.

requestBody.description: Object containing the details required to process the deletion of the specified refund identified by RES-100045. Make sure to include all necessary information to ensure a successful operation.

204.description: Delete request completed successfully with no content returned.

DeleteRefundByIdRequest.description: This schema represents the request body for deleting a refund operation. It is a string type, typically containing necessary identifiers or parameters required for the deletion action.

DeleteRefundByIdResponse_204.description: Response schema for the DELETE operation on refunds, returning no content with relevant metadata.

responseId.description: Unique identifier for the response generated by the server.

correlationId.description: Identifier used to correlate multiple requests for tracking purposes.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the response was generated.

processingRegion.description: The region where the processing of the request took place.

X-Endpoint-Id.description: Unique identifier for the endpoint associated with the request, which can be used for tracing and debugging purposes.

X-Runtime-App.description: Identifier for the application that processed the request, useful for tracking the source of the request in multi-application environments.

bearerAuth.description: This security scheme uses a bearer token based on the JSON Web Token (JWT) format for authentication. Clients must include the token in the Authorization header of their requests to gain access to secured endpoints.
